title: GS1 Web Vocabulary
usedFor: Supply-chain identifiers (GTIN, GLN) and general product attributes. Candidate `gs1:` prefix for this project's JSON-LD context.
licence: Apache License 2.0. Confirmed 2026-08-11 two ways from GS1's own repository (`github.com/gs1/WebVoc`): the `LICENSE` file itself, and the README stating verbatim "The GS1 Web vocabulary is released under an Apache 2.0 licence." Fully compatible with this project's own Apache-2.0 licensing — redistributing the term identifier and definition with attribution carries no copyleft risk.
source: https://ref.gs1.org/voc/gtin — fetched and read directly (a client-rendered page; a naive HTTP-only fetch under-renders it, a real browser was needed).
finding: `gs1:gtin`'s own definition, verbatim: "A Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) is the 14 digit GS1 Identification Key used to identify products. The key comprises a GS1 Company Prefix followed by an Item Reference Number and a Check Digit." Status: stable. Range `xsd:string`. Recorded as `skos:exactMatch` to `schema:gtin14` and `skos:closeMatch` (not exact) to `schema:gtin13/12/8` — GS1's own model already treats the 14-digit form as canonical and shorter forms as related-but-distinct. That matches `crates/dpp-domain/src/identifier/gtin/key.rs` exactly: `Gtin` requires 14 ASCII digits with a verified mod-10 check digit, and explicitly tests that a valid EAN-13 zero-padded to 14 digits parses (`prepend_zero_to_valid_ean13_gives_valid_gtin14`) — same canonical-form-plus-related-forms shape GS1 describes. **Re-checked 2026-10-13 from the repository only:** github.com/gs1/WebVoc still reports Apache-2.0 and has no commit after 2026-01-29, so nothing it holds changed after the reading above. The `gtin` page itself was not read again. The `Gtin` type described above has moved to the path now named, and still normalises the 8, 12, 13 and 14 digit forms to 14 digits.
nextStep: Read further GS1 terms one at a time, and list each in `terms` before it is emitted. `gtin` is the only one read; the rest of the namespace is refused until it is.
